failure_summary.description: Search or filter outputs were generated or retrieved but not saved as new cache results.
A follow-up providing hotel criteria or an attraction location was treated as a no-op or cache retrieval instead of an update.
Explicit return dates were modeled incorrectly or the agent asked for route details already established in the conversation.
A shared airline and class preference was applied to only the outbound flight, not the separately cached return leg.

patch.reasoning: Most failures contradict guidance already present on caching, follow-up updates, and round-trip searches, so repeating those rules is unlikely to help. The skill does not explicitly say that a shared flight preference must be applied independently to every cached leg of an itinerary; clarifying this closes the specific gap observed without broadening work to unrelated results.

edits.target: - On each turn, consider the full conversation and cached result summaries. Reuse cached results only when their domain and subject match the request. If the user adds criteria, retrieve the closest compatible result, apply the matching filter, and save the updated result. Do not filter unrelated results; search for a requested entity or category that the cached results do not cover. Avoid retrieving unrelated results or repeating constraints in filters that were already applied. Save each newly generated search or transformation result under a unique cache key. Use “No planning needed” only when cached results already satisfy every current request.
edits.content: For a new flight preference that applies to an explicitly requested multi-leg itinerary, filter each compatible cached leg independently using that leg’s own results, and save each updated leg under a distinct cache key; do not update only one leg.
